items.title: USN-9027-2: Linux kernel (FIPS) vulnerabilities
items.summary: Several security issues were discovered in the Linux kernel. An attacker could possibly use these to compromise the system. This update corrects flaws in the following subsystems: - x86 architecture; - Hardware monitoring drivers; - OCFS2 file system; - IPv4 networking; - Ethernet bridge; - Netfilte

items.title: USN-9091-1: Linux kernel (NVIDIA Tegra) vulnerabilities
items.summary: It was discovered that some AMD processors did not properly perform Reverse Map Table (RMP) checks when the IOMMU accessed certain host buffers. A local attacker with hypervisor access could possibly use this to trigger an out-of-bounds condition and compromise the integrity of SEV-SNP guest memory.

items.title: USN-9090-1: Apache HTTP Server vulnerabilities
items.summary: Zhenpeng Lin discovered that Apache HTTP Server's mod_dav module incorrectly calculated memory sizes when handling WebDAV locks. An attacker with permission to create WebDAV locks could possibly use this issue to cause Apache HTTP Server to crash, resulting in a denial of service. (CVE-2026-42528) I

items.title: USN-9068-1: Debian-LAN vulnerability
items.summary: Wolfgang Schweer discovered that Debian-LAN configured overly permissive ACLs for the Kerberos admin server. An authenticated user could possibly use this issue to change the credentials of other users, leading to privilege escalation.

items.title: USN-9089-1: x11vnc vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that x11vnc created shared memory segments with insecure permissions. A local attacker could possibly use this issue to obtain sensitive information or modify screen contents.

items.title: USN-9088-1: TigerVNC vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that the TigerVNC viewer stored TLS certificate exceptions as trusted certificate authorities. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to impersonate any VNC server after a user had added a certificate exception for the attacker's server.

items.title: USN-9087-1: signing-party vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that the gpg-key2ps tool in signing-party did not properly sanitize user IDs before passing them to a shell. If a user were tricked into processing a specially crafted OpenPGP key, an attacker could possibly use this issue to execute arbitrary commands.

items.title: USN-9086-1: SA-Exim vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that SA-Exim unsafely evaluated the parameters of its greylisting SpamAssassin rule. An attacker able to write SpamAssassin configuration files or rules could possibly use this issue to execute arbitrary code.

items.title: USN-9085-1: Ruby OpenID vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that Ruby OpenID sent a request to the claimed identifier URL before verifying the signature of an OpenID response. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to perform server-side request forgery attacks.

items.title: USN-9084-1: Radicale vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that Radicale did not delay failed authentication attempts when using htpasswd authentication. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to obtain user passwords through timing or brute-force attacks.
